# Keep the Teaching Version

**Decision.** Keep `labs/04_classes/` — the hand-written `HttpRequest` / `CorrectHttpRequest` /
`MalformedHttpRequest` hierarchy — in the tree alongside `weblog.LogEntry`, which does the same job
better and is what everything else actually imports.

**Date.** 2026-07-25, [[python-programming-laboratories]].

## Why

> "`weblog.LogEntry` is the version the rest of the repository uses; the classes here are the teaching
> version, kept because writing the special methods by hand is the exercise."
> — Python-Programming-Laboratories/labs/04_classes/README.md, 2026-07-25

The two are not competing implementations where one won. `weblog.LogEntry` is
`@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)` — the decorator generates `__eq__` and `__hash__` consistently
and blocks mutation, in one line. The lab-04 classes write `__eq__` (returning `NotImplemented` for
foreign types), an explicit `__hash__`, `total_ordering`, and a `from_line` classmethod factory by
hand. See [[pythons-data-model]].

Deleting the hand-written version once the dataclass exists would delete the **reason the dataclass
is correct**. The generated version is only trustworthy to someone who knows what it generates.

## What makes it safe rather than confusing

The redundancy is **declared and directional**. The README states which one is authoritative and why
the other exists, in the directory where a reader would otherwise be misled. An undocumented second
implementation is a trap; a labelled one is a reference.

This is [[dual-implementation-as-cross-check]] applied for pedagogy rather than verification, and a
close relative of [[keep-the-superseded-version-in-tree]] — with the difference that nothing here is
superseded. Both remain correct; only one is used.

## Alternatives rejected

| Option | Why not |
|---|---|
| **Delete lab 04 after extracting `weblog`** | destroys the exercise the lab exists to record |
| **Rewrite lab 04 to import `LogEntry`** | the whole point is writing the dunders by hand |
| **Leave both with no note** | a reader cannot tell which is authoritative — the actual failure mode |

**TODO:** only the reason for keeping it is evidenced. The three rejections above state what the
alternatives are, not that they were deliberated.

## The residual hazard

`labs/04_classes/requests.py` shadows the `requests` package that labs 10 and 11 import, if that
directory ever lands on `sys.path`. `confidence: high` — a real cost of keeping a parallel tree, and
the one thing about this decision that is not free. See [[beautifulsoup]].
